findings.evidence: The redesign case supplies only "evals/files/incident-review.md", whose image is `![bg right:40%](img/latency-chart.png)`. Reading skills/marp-slide/evals/files/img/latency-chart.png returned ENOENT. The gradient case likewise supplies only a template and reference while requiring photos/hero.jpg, photos/before.png and photos/after.png. These cases cannot complete the prescribed image-resolution and visual-validation checks from the supplied inputs.
findings.fix: Bundle the incident chart and three keynote photos under evals/files/, and include them in the respective files lists with staging paths that preserve the Markdown-relative image locations. Alternatively, explicitly make missing-image handling the expected outcome rather than expecting a completed image deck.

findings.evidence: Fallback validation requires "theme: default with the template <style> block intact (or gaia/uncover...)". However, references/theme-css-guide.md:20 instructs custom-theme users to delete that block and set `theme: name`. The built-in-theme branch also conflicts with the unconditional `lead` requirement at line 39: references/marp-syntax.md:36 says only gaia defines lead among the built-ins. Following these supported branches produces decks that the skill's own lint rejects.
findings.fix: Branch validation explicitly by deck mode: bundled templates require theme: default and embedded CSS; built-in themes require their actual supported classes; registered custom themes require valid theme metadata and registration but may omit embedded CSS. Apply lead only when the selected theme defines it, or supply a matching rule.

findings.evidence: `section:last-of-type { border-bottom: none; }` also appears in template-dark.md and template-colorful.md. Because each Marp slide occupies its own SVG, this selector matches every slide's section rather than just the final slide, removing the border from every non-lead slide. This contradicts the skill's own warning about positional section selectors.
findings.fix: Replace the positional selector in all three templates with an explicit `section.final` rule and apply `<!-- _class: final -->` only to the intended final slide. Tell the authoring workflow to preserve or relocate that directive when replacing sample slides, combining it with other required classes.
